rules.description: Fail only on a reachable, locally visible mismatch with a std raw-storage operation's documented preconditions: a raw slice exceeds its originating live allocation, assumed-initialized storage includes unwritten elements or invalid values, or ownership reconstruction uses the wrong original allocator/layout/capacity or creates a second owner. Trace the originating allocation, actual element type, offsets, writes/initialized count, length/capacity units, ownership transfer and cleanup. Give a concrete permitted input/path and the exact violated requirement. Do not duplicate obvious rustc/Clippy shapes such as directly zeroing an invalid type, directly forming a null reference, or publishing Vec capacity without any writes. Defects caused specifically by unwind belong to rust-unsafe-unwind-state; foreign pointer contracts and Python references belong to their dedicated rules.
exceptions: An enforced check or locally established construction invariant satisfies the operation-specific requirements, including exact initialized prefix, live single-allocation extent and matching ownership/deallocation layout.

Storage remains MaybeUninit until successful initialization; partial initialized storage may intentionally leak owned resources without reading or dropping unwritten values. Padding need not be initialized to create an otherwise valid value.

A bounded borrowed view does not retake ownership; a raw sentinel is never dereferenced or converted into an invalid reference. Correct same-allocator reconstruction preserves the actual original capacity/layout and single owner.
An unsafe caller contract genuinely assigns an otherwise uncontradicted obligation to the caller; report only a locally demonstrable internal violation, not an absent proof about unknown callers.

rules.description: Fail only when visible std ownership/drop semantics and state transitions establish that a permitted safe callback, safe trait operation, panic, or forgotten restoration guard can leave cleanup, reentry or subsequent safe use accessing moved-out/uninitialized storage or destroying an owner twice. Trace raw read/move, published length, every owned local, the callback boundary, restoration and exact unwind cleanup. Treat arbitrary safe Fn/FnMut/FnOnce callbacks as potentially panicking; safe trait laws and Drop execution are not unsafe contracts. Name a concrete allowed callback behavior and the invalid state it exposes. Mere business inconsistency, resource leakage or lock poisoning is not a memory-safety violation. Do not invent custom destructor behavior or hidden guard semantics.
exceptions: Publish only fully initialized owned state, or put the container in a valid empty/remaining-prefix state before moving ownership across a user callback; unwind then drops each live owner at most once.

A visible valid-state guard maintains memory safety on unwind and the API remains memory-safe if safe code forgets that guard; destruction alone must not be the only protection against invalid published state.
The exact operation between temporary raw move and restoration is locally proven nonpanicking, with no user/trait callback or potentially panicking indexing/allocation in that window.

An intentional leak-safe policy leaves raw storage or ManuallyDrop ownership unpublished on panic/forget, with no subsequent access or second destruction of the leaked resource. Resource leakage alone is not UB.
A process-abort policy is explicitly guaranteed for the relevant configuration and every pertinent panic path; do not infer panic=abort from absent configuration or treat poisoning as that guarantee.

rules.description: Fail when unsafe use of a foreign raw pointer visibly contradicts its supplied foreign API contract or locally established storage: nullness (including null zero-length slices), NUL termination for CStr::from_ptr, live initialized single-allocation extent, lifetime or foreign retention, alignment, writable out-parameters, or ownership and matching free responsibility. Cover pointers returned by foreign calls, pointers/lengths in out-parameter structs, and pointers passed to foreign consumers. Trace allocation/owner, return status, initialized out-parameters, pointer conversion and foreign release. A contract must be supplied or established by local construction: absent foreign guarantees alone are not a failure. State the concrete contradiction; do not infer ownership from an API name. Python object reference semantics belong to rust-unsafe-pyo3-reference-ownership.
exceptions: Explicit null/status handling avoids pointer conversion on failure, and null empty buffers become empty Rust slices without calling from_raw_parts on null.
Supplied foreign contracts or local construction establish NUL termination, initialization, extent, alignment and validity for the full Rust borrow or retained foreign use.
Foreign-owned storage is copied or borrowed while live and released exactly once by its documented matching foreign release function; it is not reconstructed with an incompatible Rust allocator.
A valid mutable initialized out-parameter is inspected only after a success status that guarantees its fields.
An unsafe caller obligation genuinely covers otherwise uncontradicted pointer validity; missing external contract evidence alone passes this strict rule.

rules.description: Fail on a visible mismatch between a CPython/PyO3 raw-object-pointer contract and reference handling: from_owned_ptr(_or_err/_or_opt) consumes a borrowed reference without a preceding ownership transfer or INCREF; from_borrowed_ptr(_or_err/_or_opt) increments an already new reference without balancing the original ownership; a raw or Borrowed reference is used after its owning object may be released; or cast_unchecked/cast_into_unchecked is performed without an established compatible type check or construction invariant. Distinguish Bound::from_borrowed_ptr, which acquires a strong reference, from Borrowed::from_ptr, which does not. Trace the C API's new/borrowed/stolen reference semantics, null/error handling, every INCREF/DECREF and Python callback that can release an owner. Reference-balance mismatches are in scope even when the immediate effect is a leak. Missing semantics for an unknown foreign API are not evidence of a mismatch; known CPython APIs retain their documented contracts.
exceptions: A new reference is consumed exactly once with an owned constructor, or an explicit INCREF creates the ownership consumed by that constructor.
A borrowed pointer becomes a Bound strong reference before any owner-release or Python reentry; alternatively its owner is visibly kept alive and unchanged for the entire Borrowed use.
An extra reference acquired from an already owned pointer is balanced by releasing the original reference exactly once.
A checked cast, dominating CPython type predicate, or compatible concrete construction establishes the type used by an unchecked cast.
A documented unsafe caller ownership/type obligation is uncontradicted; unknown external reference semantics alone pass this strict mismatch rule.
